about: How Titan reads SEC EDGAR without asking a model for anything it cannot know. A local model does not know a company's CIK (it invented 320196 for Apple, whose CIK is 320193, and 0001564590 for S&P Global, whose CIK is 64040), so code looks the CIK up in the SEC's own company list, reads the filing list, chooses the filings that fit the question by form and 8-K item, and reads those documents (the 8-K's Exhibit 99 press releases first). Every step is logged; the company list and every filing read are archived like any other source.

item_groups.why: 8-K Item 1.01 (material agreement), 2.01 (acquisition or disposal completed), 7.01 and 8.01 (announcements); S-4 and 425 (merger documents)
8-K Items 7.01 and 8.01 carry the company's announcements as Exhibit 99 press releases; 1.01 and 2.01 deals; 2.05 restructuring costs
8-K Item 2.02 (results of operations: the earnings release is Exhibit 99.1), and the 10-Q or 10-K for the period
8-K Item 5.02 (departure or appointment of officers and directors) and the proxy statement
the 10-K describes the business, its segments, headcount and risks
